title: See What Eye See
dna: Charity awareness campaign x Pixar-lit 3D mascot
lane: A black screen speaks two lines of copy one at a time over a dim lamp-lit room, then a 3D eyeball mascot in an armchair lands with a brush-script headline and two entry buttons into a vision-loss simulator.
why: The page withholds the product: the first four seconds are only sentences ('You can still drive. You can still read. Until one day, you can't.'), each wiped in and out on black with a lamp barely glowing behind. Only after the copy has made the point does the light come up on the mascot and the headline. The brush face and the pink-on-amber palette keep a heavy subject (vision loss) approachable.
borrow: Let two or three timed lines of copy do the opening before any image; the reveal of the hero then reads as the answer
Light the hero up out of the dark instead of fading it in: the scene was there all along
Give an experience page explicit entry buttons rather than pretending it scrolls
leave: The page does not scroll at all: nothing below the fold to reach without a click
Brush display type at hero scale only works for a campaign voice
sig: A copy-only intro on black that ends by lighting the 3D mascot already sitting in the dark room.
motion: Intro: text lines appear and wipe out one by one at centre (~1 s each) over a near-black frame where only a lamp glows. Hero: the room brightens, the eyeball character in its chair comes up, headline and CTA pills settle in. After that the page is static under the wheel; the simulator lives behind the two buttons (WebGL, three.js).
